headline: Perfect Manchester City open three-point Premier League lead
dek: City’s 5-3 win over Sunderland took them to 15 points from five matches, while Arsenal’s defeat at Brighton left the leaders with early separation at the top.

sections.heading: City capitalise as Arsenal stumble
paragraphs: Manchester City remain perfect through five Premier League matches, with Sunday’s 5-3 victory over Sunderland preserving their winning start and establishing a three-point lead. City have 15 points and a goal difference of plus eight.

The gap opened because Arsenal’s four-match winning run ended in a 3-0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion. Arsenal stay second on 12 points, but the result brought Brighton into the leading group rather than allowing the top two to continue together.

sections.heading: Brighton surge into third
paragraphs: Brighton are third with 10 points and a goal difference of plus 11 after their victory over Arsenal. That places them two points behind the side they beat and one ahead of both Brentford and Leeds United.

Brentford’s 3-0 win over Chelsea lifted their total to nine points and fourth place, ahead of Leeds on goal difference. Leeds also have nine after a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace, but their plus-four goal difference trails Brentford’s plus six.

sections.heading: Away wins shape the middle ground
paragraphs: Aston Villa, Liverpool and Coventry City supplied the round’s three away victories. Villa won 3-2 at Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool edged AFC Bournemouth 1-0 and Coventry took a 1-0 result from Nottingham Forest.
Elsewhere, Everton beat Ipswich Town 1-0 and Newcastle United defeated Hull City 2-1. Fulham and Manchester United drew 1-1, completing a round in which eight of the 10 fixtures produced a winner.

sections.heading: Coventry win but remain in the bottom three
paragraphs: Coventry’s victory at Nottingham Forest was not enough to move them out of 18th place. They have three points from five matches and a goal difference of minus nine.

Fulham remain winless and sit 19th with two points after their draw against Manchester United. Tottenham are also without a victory and occupy 20th place on two points, with their 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa leaving them below Fulham on goal difference.
